reference.name: Text Contains filters interpret literal percent and underscore as SQL wildcards
reference.summary: Ordinary UI Contains and Does not contain filters interpret typed percent and underscore as SQL wildcard syntax, including records without the typed punctuation or excluding them incorrectly.
reference.expected: The UI text operators should match the entered text literally, case-insensitively, rather than expose undocumented SQL wildcard syntax. This expectation concerns conversion of UI values; raw API pattern operators retain their intended wildcard semantics.
reference.actual: Name Contains QA% matches QA Alpha and QA Beta although neither name contains a percent sign. Job Title Does not contain 50% excludes a person whose title is 50 off, without a percent sign. Underscore also acts as a one-character wildcard. Ordinary-text controls return the expected records.
reproSteps: Create fresh People with a unique common name prefix, for example QA Alpha and QA Beta, with neither name containing a percent sign.
Apply Name > Contains > QA%. Observe names lacking the literal percent sign still included. Compare an ordinary matching prefix and a nonexistent prefix.
Give a fresh person Job Title 50 off, without a percent sign. Apply Job Title > Does not contain > 50%. Observe the person incorrectly excluded despite not containing that literal text.
Compare a record actually containing a percent sign and ordinary-text filters. Repeat on fresh data; saving and reloading the filtered view retains the pattern behavior.
For underscore, compare names differing by one character and apply a Contains value with an underscore in that position; observe the underscore acts as a wildcard rather than requiring the character.

knownHits.reason: Matches literal percent and underscore being interpreted as wildcards in text Contains filters. The workflow object is an insignificant variation of the same filtering path.

reference.name: Renaming a favorited record leaves its sidebar label and tooltip stale across reloads
reference.summary: A completed record rename does not refresh the favorite’s cached sidebar label or tooltip, including after ordinary reload.
reference.expected: A favorite should display the current saved record name after renaming and reload, while continuing to navigate to that record.
reference.actual: Record header, breadcrumb and index display the saved new name, but the expanded sidebar favorite and collapsed tooltip retain the old name across reloads. Clicking the favorite still opens the correct record.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Task with a distinctive title and add it to Favorites.
Rename the Task and wait for saving to complete. Confirm its header, breadcrumb and index show the new title.
Compare the favorite’s expanded sidebar label and collapsed-sidebar tooltip; both still show the old title.
Reload and observe the stale favorite name persists while the record title remains correctly saved.
Controls: favorite a record only after renaming to get the correct label; remove and re-add the affected favorite or clear the disposable browser metadata cache and reload to recover.

knownHits.reason: Matches a favorited record retaining its old sidebar name after a completed rename and reload. Renaming a Workflow instead of a Task reaches the same failure.
